formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with allyl alcohol (poly(allyl alcohol), PAA) at 195/273K with t-butyl hydroperoxide initiator; one of three vinyl-monomer/SO2 alternating copolymers studied as EO-free polymer-electrolyte hosts (Fig. 4).
formulations.Notes: Radical copolymerization of SO2 with vinyl monomers is generally alternating 1:1, so Comonomer percentage set to 50. Salt loading is 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomer-unit concentration. Text: RT conductivity does not exceed 1e-8 S/cm (stated bound, not exact); numeric conductivity fields left null. About two orders of magnitude lower ambient conductivity than PVA-SO2 analogue (Fig. 4).
formulations.Reference: Przyluski, J.; Wieczorek, W. "Copolymer electrolytes." Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with vinyl acetate (poly(vinyl acetate), PVA) at 195/273K with t-butyl hydroperoxide initiator; one of three vinyl-monomer/SO2 alternating copolymers studied as EO-free polymer-electrolyte hosts (Fig. 4).
formulations.Notes: Comonomer percentage=50 assuming alternating 1:1 SO2/vinyl-monomer structure. Salt loading is 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomer-unit concentration. Conductivity values are approximate order-of-magnitude figures from text ('increases from 1e-6 S/cm at room T to 1e-5 S/cm at 373K'); room T assumed ~25C, 373K=100C. About two orders of magnitude higher conductivity than PAA-SO2, attributed to higher chain flexibility.
formulations.Reference: Przyluski, J.; Wieczorek, W. "Copolymer electrolytes." Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with acrylamide (polyacrylamide, PAAM) at 195/273K with t-butyl hydroperoxide initiator; one of three vinyl-monomer/SO2 alternating copolymers studied as EO-free polymer-electrolyte hosts (Fig. 4); reported as one of the highest-conductivity polymer electrolytes not containing polyether units known to authors at the time.
formulations.Notes: Comonomer percentage=50 assuming alternating 1:1 structure. Salt loading is 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomer-unit concentration. Text: RT conductivity 'exceeded 1e-5 S/cm' (stated lower bound), ~1 order of magnitude higher than pristine PEO-LiClO4; attributed to cooperative N/O dipole interactions. All SO2-based electrolytes stable up to 373K.
formulations.Reference: Przyluski, J.; Wieczorek, W. "Copolymer electrolytes." Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Undoped EO-SO2 copolymer (aliphatic polysulfite obtained by ionic copolymerization of SO2 with ethylene oxide at room temperature, ref. [9]); reported to be amorphous prior to salt doping.
formulations.Notes: Exact EO:SO2 ratio not stated numerically, so Comonomer percentage left null. No quantitative Tg/Tm reported for the undoped copolymer; text states only that it is amorphous, in contrast to the crystalline complex formed upon lithium salt addition (Fig. 6).
formulations.Reference: Przyluski, J.; Wieczorek, W. "Copolymer electrolytes." Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: EO-SO2 copolymer (aliphatic polysulfite) doped with LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomeric unit concentration (Fig. 5, Fig. 6 DSC).
formulations.Notes: Fig.6 DSC peaks (229K, 312K) tentatively assigned as Tg(-44C)/Tm(39C); source labels them generically 'Peak1/Peak2'. A ~382K event ('Trough') not assigned, possibly decomposition. Text: high heat of melting suggests strong complexation; crystalline unlike amorphous undoped copolymer, but unstable over time unless PEO-blended (ref.[9]). Conductivity (30C,50C) digitized from Fig.5 'x' series; consistent with text's >1e-6 S/cm ambient claim.
formulations.Reference: Przyluski, J.; Wieczorek, W. "Copolymer electrolytes." Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076.

formulations.Notes: Conductivity digitized from Fig. 5 '+' (LiBF4) series. Text: ambient conductivity for both EO-SO2 salt systems exceeds 1e-6 S/cm; samples thermally stable to ~373K. DSC (Fig.6) reported only for LiClO4 analogue; Tg/Tm/crystallinity not stated for this LiBF4 variant, left null.
